Updated assessment with SLOOS overlay:
- Baseline (FOMC statement): Neutral with a slight dovish tilt—rates on hold, inflation below target, and ongoing T-bill purchases/repo operations framed as implementation support rather than QE.
- SLOOS signal on credit supply: Banks reported tighter standards for C&I loans and construction/land development loans, tightened other terms across firm sizes, increased credit score thresholds, and tightened credit limits. Banks also indicated reduced risk tolerance and broadly expect tighter standards in 2020 across riskier categories (including C&I, multifamily CRE, and construction).
- SLOOS signal on credit demand/quality: Demand was weaker in construction and some consumer segments, with several categories unchanged; banks expect deterioration in loan portfolios, collateral values, and HELOCs.
- Implications: The tightening in lending standards and softer demand convey a negative credit impulse that adds downside risk to growth and inflation, reinforcing the case for continued accommodation and caution. Compared with the FSR-only adjustment, SLOOS tilts the outlook more cautiously by signaling a headwind from bank intermediation.

Net: Supportive policy and strong labor markets keep the tone from turning negative, but SLOOS-driven tightening warrants a further downward adjustment from the prior +0.15.
